original.target_description: Experiment 1 job-choice target-option frequency under Control versus Regret-Salient conditions; within-condition binomial tests and between-condition comparison located, but assigned contrast unresolved.

n.sample_role: Candidate analytic participant counts only: Control 23, Regret-Salient 39, between-condition comparison 62; no unique target count selected.
n.exclusions: No subjects chose the decoy option. No choice-analysis exclusions reported in §2.2.1; target-specific denominator unresolved.
n.location: Experiment 1, §2.1.1 and §2.2.1 (Experimental effects on choice frequencies), Table 2 discussion
n.quote:
Twenty out of 23 (87%) Control subjects
                        chose the targeted option, but only 24 out of 39 (61.5%) of the
                        Regret-Salient subjects did so, χ 2 (1, N = 62) = 4.54,
                        Fisher’s exact test p = .04, φ 2 =
                        .07. ... The decoy effect was significant in the Control condition (i.e., the
                        percentage of subjects choosing the targeted option was larger than 50%),
                        exact binomial p = .000. No significant decoy effect was
                        found in the Regret-Salient condition, exact binomial p =
                            .20.

notes:
Identity independently verified from the supplied canonical Cambridge Core web text: title Regret salience and accountability in the decoyeffect; Terry Connolly, Jochen Reb, Edgar E. Kausel; Judgment and Decision Making, Volume 8, Issue 2, March 2013, pp. 136–149; DOI 10.1017/S1930297500005064. Primary research article with Experiment 1 methods, results and discussion, Experiment 2 and general discussion present; not merely an abstract or secondary report. The page separately lists online publication on 01 January 2023. No PDF supplied; no PDF rendering possible. HTML sections used as precise locations; printed p.4 cannot be verified from HTML layout. Both assigned rows supply identical Study 1 descriptions and p.4 locators. Experiment 1 has no no-decoy experimental arm: both choice sets contain a decoy, and the manipulation is regret salience. Relevant choice candidates are (a) Control target-choice frequency versus 50%, exact binomial p = .000, printed analytic group count 23; (b) Regret-Salient target-choice frequency versus 50%, exact binomial p = .20, printed analytic group count 39; and (c) between-condition target-choice comparison, printed χ 2 (1, N = 62) = 4.54, with Fisher’s exact test p = .04 and φ 2 = .07. The Fisher p is explicitly a different named test from the printed chi-square statistic; no chi-square p is explicitly supplied. No binomial test statistic is printed in this passage. The supplied description does not identify an arm or uniquely select a contrast; rows cannot be assigned to candidates by their order or by numeric values. All candidates remain in notes; no target-specific positive values are entered. N = 62 is explicitly printed for the between-condition comparison; 23 and 39 are explicitly printed denominators of the within-condition choice frequencies. No analytic N is inferred from recruitment totals or degrees of freedom, and no N sum or effect conversion is performed.                         × 2 (Choice Set: Set 1 vs. Set 2) fully between-subjects factorial.
